name: Steak au Poivre Nihari
description: A halal French-Pakistani fusion recipe: pepper-crusted beef sirloin seared to medium-rare, served over a slow-reduced nihari jus made with marrow bones, long pepper, mace, and hing. Steak au poivre nihari bridges two culinary traditions without diluting either.
keywords: steak au poivre nihari, nihari steak, french pakistani beef steak, peppered steak nihari jus, halal steak recipe, halal beef steak
recipeIngredient: 500 g beef marrow bones, cut into 5 cm rounds
300 g beef shin or shank, bone-in
1 tsp fine sea salt, plus more to taste
1 tbsp whole wheat flour (atta), dissolved in 3 tbsp cold water
15 g cold unsalted butter for jus
2 halal beef sirloin or ribeye steaks, each 250 g, at least 2.5 cm thick
½ tsp coarsely cracked long pepper (pipli)
2 garlic cloves, skin on, lightly crushed

recipeInstructions.name: Blanch the bones
recipeInstructions.text: Place marrow bones and beef shin in a cold pot, cover with cold water, bring to a boil, drain, and rinse under cold water.

recipeInstructions.name: Char the onion
recipeInstructions.text: Char the onion halves cut-side down over a gas flame or under a hot grill until deeply blackened on the cut surface.

recipeInstructions.name: Toast the spices
recipeInstructions.text: Heat 1 tbsp oil in a heavy pot over medium heat. Add peppercorns, pipli, fennel, cumin, both cardamoms, mace, and cassia. Stir for 45 seconds.

recipeInstructions.name: Add hing and ginger-garlic paste
recipeInstructions.text: Add hing, stir for five seconds, then add ginger-garlic paste and cook for two minutes until the raw smell is gone.

recipeInstructions.name: Simmer the jus
recipeInstructions.text: Add blanched bones, charred onion, salt, nihari masala, and 1.2 litres water. Bring to a gentle boil then simmer partially covered for 2 hours.

recipeInstructions.name: Strain and thicken the jus
recipeInstructions.text: Strain the stock, return to a clean pan, whisk in the atta-water slurry, and reduce to about 250 ml until it coats a spoon.

recipeInstructions.name: Dry-brine the steaks
recipeInstructions.text: Pat steaks dry, salt with flaky sea salt, and rest uncovered on a rack in the refrigerator for at least one hour.

recipeInstructions.name: Crust the steaks
recipeInstructions.text: Mix cracked black pepper and cracked pipli and press firmly onto both flat faces of each steak.

recipeInstructions.name: Sear the steaks
recipeInstructions.text: Heat a cast-iron skillet until smoking, add oil, and sear steaks for 2.5 to 3 minutes per side for medium-rare (52–54°C internal).

recipeInstructions.name: Baste with butter
recipeInstructions.text: In the final 30 seconds, add butter, garlic, and thyme to the pan and baste the steaks continuously.

recipeInstructions.name: Rest the steaks
recipeInstructions.text: Transfer steaks to a warm plate and rest for five minutes.

recipeInstructions.name: Finish the jus and plate
recipeInstructions.text: Warm the nihari jus over medium-low heat, whisk in cold butter, spoon onto warmed plates, and place the steak on or beside the jus. Finish with a pinch of flaky salt.
